mathematical_explanation: The proof correctly establishes the essential nonautomatic point: coset multiplication is well-defined. In node 3, the displayed factorization of (ab)^{-1}(a'b') is correct, normality places the conjugate b^{-1}(a^{-1}a')b in N, and subgroup closure places the product in N. Node 4 omits explicit checks of the remaining group axioms, but these are standard short inherited verifications: closure is built into the definition, associativity follows from associativity in G, N is the identity coset, and a^{-1}N is the inverse of aN. Under the stated ordinary-textbook rubric, those implicit inferences are sufficient.
